clue.text: Designer of buildings to keep one dry in 9?

indicators.note: a holder keeps something within it, so the architect's name goes around the other pieces

parts.note: Sir Christopher Wren, architect of St Paul's Cathedral
one is the Roman numeral I
TT, teetotal, is crossword shorthand for a non-drinker

explanation.surface: An architect is asked to keep a person sheltered from the rain within some black and white setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 is BLACK AND WHITE, so 'in 9' means 'in black and white', the idiom for set down on paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: something in black and white has been put down on paper in ink.

clue.text: Shorter bursts for classical speakers

indicators.note: something that bursts breaks apart, so the letters of the word before are scattered and regrouped

explanation.surface: Brief explosive outbursts are the style of ancient orators.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: teachers and practitioners of oratory in ancient Greece and Rome were known by this term.

clue.text: Bore child, a small boy

parts.note: a tot is a small child
Ed is a short form of Edward, a boy's name

explanation.surface: A woman gave birth to a little lad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' reads as giving birth, but it is the past tense of carry.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to tote something is to carry it, so the past tense means carried.

clue.text: Better send the dancer to strip off

indicators.note: stripping off removes the outer layer, so each of the three words loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: It would be an improvement to make the performer undress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strip off' looks like the dancer's act but trims the ends of send, the and dancer, leaving EN, H and ANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to improve something is to raise its quality, as both verbs mean.

clue.text: Doubt place is beset by horrible curse

indicators.note: something beset is surrounded on all sides, so the abbreviation sits inside the other letters
horrible suggests something mangled, so the letters of curse are rearranged

parts.note: PL is the standard abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: A town is uncertain because a dreadful hex hangs over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horrible' turns CURSE into SCRUE, which then surrounds PL.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a qualm or moral hesitation is a kind of doubt about acting.

clue.text: We're told seabird is yellow

indicators.note: something we are told is heard, so the bird's name is taken by its sound

parts.note: a sea raven, a dialect name for a cormorant, a bird of the coast

explanation.surface: Apparently a bird of the coast has a yellow colouring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yellow' looks like a colour but means cowardly; said quickly, sea raven sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang sense: yellow means cowardly, and the answer means abjectly cowardly.

clue.text: Running due north and south, didn't reach target

indicators.note: running here means set in motion, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Heading straight up and down the map, someone fell short of their goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running' signals the anagram of DUE NORTH plus S.
explanation.definitionFit: Sport and archery sense: to have aimed too low or short means a shot fell before the mark.

clue.text: Two Republicans standing in the French sun, getting tans

indicators.note: in places the two pieces inside the French article and the S

parts.note: la is French for the (feminine)
S is an abbreviation for sun, as in Sunday
R is the abbreviation for Republican, so two give RR
standing means upright, or up

explanation.surface: A pair of American conservatives stand in the French sunshine getting brown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tans' looks like sunburn but means beats, as tanning a hide is thrashing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang sense: to tan someone's hide is to thrash them, just as to larrup is.

clue.text: Oddly bold account with naked cavorting, but not Fifty Shades?

indicators.note: oddly takes the odd-numbered letters, first and third, of the word bold
cavorting means leaping about, so the letters of with and naked are rearranged

explanation.surface: A racy scene of naked frolicking that isn't quite the famous erotic novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Fifty Shades of Grey is a bestselling erotic novel; the answer is the opposite of shades of grey, with no in-between tones.
explanation.definitionFit: Allusion: the novel title implies grey tones, while this phrase means stark contrasts with no middle shading.

clue.text: Order he's forgotten for cream

indicators.note: something forgotten is left out, so the pronoun drops from the longer word

parts.note: a behest is a command or order
he's reads as he is, giving the letters of the pronoun

explanation.surface: A cafe order is missing an ingredient, so someone forgot the cream.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the cream of anything is its finest part, the top of the bunch.

clue.text: Whoops welcoming Fancy Dan's fans wearing orange?

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: whoops as a noun means shouts, or hollers

indicators.note: fancy as a verb means to imagine or rework, so the name's letters are rearranged

parts.note: the name Dan; the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: Cheers greet a show-off's supporters who are dressed in orange.
explanation.walkthrough: A Fancy Dan is a show-off, but 'Fancy' rearranges DAN to AND. Orange is the Dutch national colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Dutch supporters famously wear orange at matches, and Dutch people are called by this name.

clue.text: Brown's good (and gold) to clothe yourself in

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
to don a garment is to put it on

explanation.surface: A brown fabric that is fine and golden to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown is Gordon Brown, the UK Prime Minister 2007-2010.
explanation.definitionFit: Name: the former British Prime Minister's first name, so Brown leads to his forename.

clue.text: Caught tragedy bowdlerised in 9

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
King Lear is Shakespeare's tragedy
a bowdlerised text has been censored, or cut

explanation.surface: A tragic play was censored, the black and white version caught with cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 is BLACK AND WHITE; a matter in black and white has no grey areas.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a black and white issue is unambiguous, with no room for doubt.

clue.text: People reversing around country in vehicle

indicators.note: around means one piece encloses the other
reversing means the word for people is read backwards

parts.note: a race is a people or nation
a state is a country

explanation.surface: Folk are backing up their car around the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' sounds like the car backing up, but it turns the word for people, making ECAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a British name for a station wagon, a car with a long rear load area.

clue.text: Like Scot south of Barnet coming from continental regions

indicators.note: in a down clue, south of means placed below the hairstyle

parts.note: barnet is Cockney rhyming slang for hair (Barnet Fair), here a hairstyle
as means like
Ian is a typically Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: Like a Scotsman from the south of Barnet, a north London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnet is a London borough, but in rhyming slang it means hair (Barnet Fair), here a bushy hairstyle.
explanation.definitionFit: Compound adjective: relating to both Africa and Asia, two continents, so from those regions.

clue.text: Boxes, losing tense contest in 9

indicators.note: losing means a letter is dropped from the word for boxes

parts.note: chests are boxes
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A boxer loses a tense bout in a black and white film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxes' looks like a boxer's verb but is a plural noun. 9 is BLACK AND WHITE: the board's squares.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a board game played on black and white squares between two players.

clue.text: Split, Zagreb but not great 9 thing

indicators.note: split means broken apart, so the letters are rearranged
but not means a letter is left out of the city name

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for great

explanation.surface: Two Croatian cities, Split and Zagreb, though the capital isn't great.
explanation.walkthrough: Split is a Croatian city, but here it signals the anagram of ZAREB, which is ZAGREB less G.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a striped African animal, the classic creature in black and white.

clue.text: Rip off ripe, firm bananas — they're intensely green

indicators.note: off means removed, so the first word's letters come out of the second

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
bananas is slang for crazy, or nuts

explanation.surface: Tear the peel from ripe, firm bananas, say people who are fanatically green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rip off' reads as a con, but RIP is taken from ripe, leaving E.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: environmental zealots, obsessively devoted to green causes, get this label.

clue.text: Utility bill with name and energy covering front

indicators.note: covering means wrapping around, so the outer pieces enclose the word for front

parts.note: an ad is a bill, a poster or advertisement
a tag is a name or label
E is the physics symbol for energy
the van is the front, as in vanguard

explanation.surface: A gas bill bearing a name and energy charges on the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utility' looks like gas or water but means usefulness.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: utility is usefulness, a benefit or gain.

clue.text: Tried appeal about remark by journalist

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the abbreviation for appeal is read backwards

parts.note: SA is sex appeal
a say is a remark or word
ED is the abbreviation for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter tested an appeal about a statement.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to test the quality of metal or a substance is to try it.

clue.text: More than one jade gnome's outside, say — look around

indicators.note: outside means the outer letters of the word gnome

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means

indicators.note: around means the word for look is turned backwards

parts.note: to see is to look

explanation.surface: A garden gnome made of jade is outside, so have a look round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jade' looks like the stone but is an old word for a worn-out horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a jade is a tired old horse, and this nursery word means horses.

clue.text: Silver's seemingly good grade

parts.note: pi, short for pious, means good
a rate is a grade or rank

explanation.surface: Silver apparently counts as a good grade.
explanation.walkthrough: Silver is Long John Silver of Treasure Island; 'seemingly' hints that pi rate is just a good grade.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Long John Silver of Treasure Island is the best-known sea robber in fiction.

clue.text: Fancy entertaining old fellow, fit for the opposite sex

indicators.note: entertaining means holding within, so the old fellow goes inside

parts.note: fancy means wish
a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: Fancy an old fellow putting on something suited to the other sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective: suited to or typical of women, from a man's viewpoint the other sex.

clue.text: Therefore a colour for a rose is rose?

parts.note: so means therefore
red is the classic colour of a rose

explanation.surface: A colour for a flower is the colour rose, so the clue jokingly asks.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'rose' looks like the flower or a colour, but it is the past tense of rise.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: rose, past tense of rise, means climbed or flew upward.

clue.text: Nettle from mountains, but right at the bottom

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom is the end, so the letter goes to the last place

parts.note: a range is a line of mountains

explanation.surface: A nettle growing in the mountains, though rightly down at the foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nettle' looks like the plant but is a verb meaning irk.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to nettle someone is to irritate or infuriate them.

clue.text: Month in which politician backs worker gladly

indicators.note: in which means the month holds the other pieces

parts.note: July is a month

indicators.note: backs means the politician's abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: LIB is a Liberal, a politician
an ant is a worker in crossword convention

explanation.surface: In one summer month, a politician supports a worker with delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backs' looks like supports but reverses LIB to BIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: joyfully and triumphantly, which is a stronger form of gladly.

clue.text: Grand foreign monarch's 9 mixture

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand
rey is Spanish for king; the possessive adds nothing

explanation.surface: A great king abroad has a mixture of black and white.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 is BLACK AND WHITE; mixing those gives the shade.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the shade made when black and white paint are mixed together.

clue.text: Paper splits English and German articles into pieces

indicators.note: splits means the paper's name divides the two articles

parts.note: a is the English indefinite article
der is a German definite article
the Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper tears up English and German articles.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid. 'articles' looks like news stories but means grammatical words.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: apart, broken into separate parts, as torn apart.

clue.text: Before this speech he produces a crown, perhaps

indicators.note: before this means the pronoun placed in front of the answer makes the longer word, so taken off it leaves the answer

parts.note: a headdress is something worn on the head, such as a crown
the pronoun he, taken as written

explanation.surface: Before giving this talk, a man produces a crown.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse-style subtraction: 'Before this' tells you the pronoun goes in front of the answer, and the longer word is defined by 'a crown, perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a formal speech or oration given to an audience.
